w: Coyote Valley Dam created this 1,922-acre reservoir northeast of Ukiah in 1958, damming the Russian River for flood control, water storage and hydroelectric power. Beneath it sits a Cold War-era fallout shelter, built into the dam to shelter staff from radiation in a Soviet nuclear attack.
s: A 1958 reservoir dam hiding a Cold War fallout shelter
_facts: 1,922-acre reservoir formed by Coyote Valley Dam, completed 1958
Provides flood control, water conservation, hydroelectric power and recreation
Dam includes a Cold War-era fallout shelter built against Soviet nuclear attack

w: Next to the Sun House, the redwood Craftsman home artist Grace Hudson and her husband John built in 1911. The City of Ukiah now owns and runs both museum and house, which is listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its architecture and its ties to Hudson's paintings of Pomo life.
s: A Craftsman house-turned-museum for painter Grace Hudson
_facts: Adjacent to the Sun House, built 1911 for artist Grace Hudson and husband John
Owned and operated by the City of Ukiah
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places
